Filtering based on BLAST accuracy is applied to remove OTUs with low-confidence taxonomic assignments, typically indicated by low sequence similarity (`pident`), poor alignment coverage (`qcovs`), or poor fit of the rank resolution (`evalue`) [@tedersoo2022]. Such features are frequently artefactual or biologically uninterpretable and can bias ecological inference if retained.

+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Column name                      | Definition                                                                                     |
+==================================+================================================================================================+
| query_seq                        | DNA sequence                                                                                   |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| X1st_hit                         | first BLAST hit: best match against the database                                               |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| qlen                             | query length: length of the DNA sequence                                                       |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| slen                             | length of the matching sequence in the database                                                |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| qstart                           | start point on the query sequence that matches with the database sequence                      |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| qend                             | end point on the query sequence that matches with the database sequence                        |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| sstart                           | start point on the database sequence that matches with the query sequence                      |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| send                             | end point on the database sequence that matches with the query sequence                        |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| evalue                           | summary statistic that estimate the goodness of match between the query and database sequences |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| length                           | length of the match between the query and database sequences                                   |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| nident                           | number of pairbase that match within the matching length                                       |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| mismatch                         | number of pairbase that do not match within the matching length (length - nident)              |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| gapopen                          | number of gap openings                                                                         |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| gaps                             | gap size: number of pairbase inside gaps                                                       |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| sstrand                          | orientation of the database sequence (plus or minus)                                           |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| qcovs                            | percentage of coverage of the query sequence over the database sequence (length/qlen)          |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| pident                           | percentage of identity between the two sequences (nident/length)                               |
+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

: Table 1. Definitions of BLAST results

This section documents how to filter OTUs based on BLAST results (see table above), and clean the taxonomy assignations based on BLAST accuracy, in `phyloseq` objects. Alternatively, you may copy the codes below into your own script, and use your own data.

## BLAST filtering

Filtering out OTUs based on BLAST results is normally done during bioinformatic processing, but if it was not the case for your OTU table, simple filters can be used to further remove artefacts.

Depending on primers, the expected length of amplicons varies greatly, thus it is impossible to determine a universal threshold for sequence length. However, most studies set this threshold to roughly half of the expected length (see table below).

+--------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+-----------+--------------+------------------------+---------------------------+
| Name   | Target                             | Primers (sequence 5’-3’)                | Regions   | Length\      | Threshold query length | References                |
|        |                                    |                                         |           | (average)    |                        |                           |
+========+====================================+=========================================+===========+==============+========================+===========================+
| 16S    | Prokaryotes (Bacteria and Archaea) | 515F-Y (GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA)\           | V4-V5     | 360-500 bp\  | 250 bp                 | [@parada2015]             |
|        |                                    | 926RB (CCGYCAATTYMTTTRAGTTT)            |           | (\~460 bp)   |                        |                           |
+--------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+-----------+--------------+------------------------+---------------------------+
| ITS    | Fungi                              | ITS9MUN (TGTACACACCGCCCGTCG)\           | ITS1-ITS2 | 150-1200 bp\ | 100 bp                 | [@tedersoo2016]           |
|        |                                    | ITS4ngsUni (CCTSCSCTTANTDATATGC)        |           | (\~280 bp)   |                        |                           |
+--------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+-----------+--------------+------------------------+---------------------------+
| CO1    | Metazoa                            | mlCOIintF (GGWACWGGWTGAACWGTWTAYCCYCC)\ | 320-345\  | 250-700\     | 200 bp                 | [@leray2013; @geller2013] |
|        |                                    | jgHCO2198 (TAIACYTCIGGRTGICCRAARAAYCA)  | 658       | (\~313 bp)   |                        |                           |
+--------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+-----------+--------------+------------------------+---------------------------+

: Table 2. Primer sets used for this data set

Alternatively, some studies also suggest to filter out sequences with less than 15% query coverage (`qcovs`), which are assumed to be fully synthetic [@kunjapur2018]. In these cases, even though the query sequence may be long, if it has such a low alignment with the sequences in the database, it cannot be considered natural.

Note that the threshold at a query cover of 15% was determined arbitrarily. The authors denote: "This was guided by not wanting to pick too high a level, lest we exclude natural sequences \[...\]. Similarly, we did not want to pick too low a level, since BLASTn searches preferentially for highly identical regions, and thus might cut off the end of a synthetic sequence yielding a maximal-scoring segment pair with lower query coverage and higher percentage identity (thus falsely classified as natural)" [@kunjapur2018].

This demonstration is done with the ITS data, and we choose to remove sequences with a length (`qlen`) shorter than 100 bp or a query cover (`qcovs`) smaller than 15%.

::: callout-tip
## remove_taxa

Homemade function `remove_taxa` (loaded with `001_required_packages.R`): a simplified way of removing a selection of OTU from a `phyloseq` object.

```{r}
remove_taxa <- function(badTaxa, physeq){
  allTaxa <- taxa_names(physeq)
  cleanTaxa <- allTaxa[!(allTaxa %in% badTaxa)]
  return(prune_taxa(cleanTaxa, physeq))
}
```
:::

```{r}
#| output: false
# Extract BLAST results from OTU table
BLAST_rare <- as.data.frame(otu_table_rare@tax_table) %>%
  # Convert column class automatically
  type.convert(as.is = TRUE)

# Identify artefacts based on BLAST results
otu_qlen <- filter(BLAST_rare, qlen < 100)[["taxa_OTU"]] # no sequence identified
otu_qcovs <- filter(BLAST_rare, qcovs < 15)[["taxa_OTU"]] # 3 sequences identified
```

With your own data, if you identify potential artefacts this way, inspect them before removing them to make sure that they are indeed artefacts.

```{r}
# Inspect the sequences with a low query cover
filter(BLAST_rare, taxa_OTU %in% otu_qcovs) %>%
  select(phylum, genus, qlen, qcovs, pident, evalue)

# Number of reads of these OTUs
taxa_sums(otu_table_rare)[otu_qcovs]
```

These 3 OTUs are much longer (1147 to 1638 bp) than the expected length of the amplicon (\~280 bp, see Table 2), only a small part of them matches a reference sequence (14%), and they are represented by only 1 or 2 reads. They are most likely artefacts (e.g., chimeras) and can be removed.

```{r}
#| output: false
# Filter artefacts
BLAST_filter <- filter(BLAST_rare, !taxa_OTU %in% c(otu_qlen, otu_qcovs))
otu_BLAST_filter <- remove_taxa(c(otu_qlen, otu_qcovs), otu_table_rare)

# Count OTUs before and after filtering
ntaxa(otu_table_rare) # 9039
ntaxa(otu_BLAST_filter) # 9036
```

In this demonstration, most artefacts were removed in prior steps (bioinformatic processing).

## BLAST cleaning

After filtering out any remaining potential artefacts, BLAST statistics (such as `pident` and `evalue`) can also be used to confirm taxonomic assignations. At this stage, OTUs are not removed, as they are not considered artefacts anymore, but simply unknown species. This means that, based on specific thresholds for each target gene and taxonomic rank (Table 3), any taxonomic assignation below these thresholds is replaced with `NA`.

### Unknown organisms

There are a few exceptions to this rule. As a rule of thumb (arbitrary thresholds):

1.  Any OTU with an identity (`pident`) below 70% cannot be identified, even up to the kingdom level [@tedersoo2014].
2.  Any OTU with an e-value (`evalue`) above e^-20^ cannot be identified, even up to the kingdom level [@tedersoo2014].
3.  Any OTU with a query coverage (`qcovs`) below 50% must be investigated [@kunjapur2018].
4.  OTUs with an e-value between e^-20^ and e^-50^ should be manually checked against the 10 best BLAST matches for accurate assignment [@tedersoo2014].

These OTUs should be further investigated to determine if they should be removed or preserved.

```{r}
#| output: false
# Identify unknown OTUs
BLAST_unknown <- filter(BLAST_filter, pident < 70 | evalue > 1e-50 | qcovs < 50)
nrow(BLAST_unknown) # 1078 OTUs

# How many reads do they represent?
sum(taxa_sums(otu_BLAST_filter)[BLAST_unknown$taxa_OTU]) # 5474 reads (~1.5%)
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Look at the unknown OTUs
View(BLAST_unknown)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
BLAST_unknown_vis <- select(BLAST_unknown, kingdom:species, query_seq:pident)

truncate_cols <- c("query_seq", "taxa_OTU", "BLAST_ID")
idx <- match(truncate_cols, names(BLAST_unknown_vis)) - 1  # DT uses 0-based indices

datatable(
  head(BLAST_unknown_vis, n=100),
  options = list(
    scrollX = TRUE,
    pageLength = 10,
    columnDefs = list(
      list(
        targets = idx,
        render = JS(
          "function(data, type, row, meta) {",
          "  if (type !== 'display' || data === null) return data;",
          "  data = data.toString();",
          "  return data.length > 8 ?",
          "    '<span title=\"' + data.replace(/\"/g, '&quot;') + '\">' + data.substr(0, 8) + '…</span>' :",
          "    data;",
          "}"
        )
      )
    )
  ),
  rownames = FALSE
)
```

To which phyla were these OTUs assigned?

```{r}
# Number of unknown OTUs per phylum ("." = no assignation)
sort(table(BLAST_unknown$phylum), decreasing = TRUE)
```

In a smaller data set, these OTUs could be investigated one by one: a manual check against the 10 best BLAST matches allows for an accurate assignment. To do so, make sure to use the same database as the one used to generate your OTU table in the first place. For example, the OTU tables for each target gene were generated using the following databases:

- [SILVA](https://www.arb-silva.de) for Bacteria and Archaea (16S)
- [UNITE](https://unite.ut.ee/analysis.php) for the eukaryotic nuclear ribosomal ITS region
- [BOLD](https://id.boldsystems.org/) identification engine for animal identification (CO1)

OTUs that cannot be confidently identified as Fungi could then be removed.

::: callout-tip
**Create a FASTA file**

To manually BLAST all sequences at once, create a FASTA file from your sequences and OTU ID, using the R package `Biostrings`.

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Extract sequences
fasta_seqs <- DNAStringSet(BLAST_unknown$query_seq)

# Name sequences with OTU ID
names(fasta_seqs) <- BLAST_unknown$taxa_OTU

# Write FASTA file
writeXStringSet(fasta_seqs, "BLAST_unknown.fasta")
```
:::

Here, more than 1000 OTUs fall in this category, which makes a manual check impractical. Many of them belong to groups of fungi that are poorly represented in reference databases, such as Rozellomycota and Zoopagomycota, which explains why their BLAST matches are weak. Together, they represent only \~1.5% of the reads. We therefore keep these OTUs, but we do not trust their taxonomy below the kingdom level: their assignation at all ranks below kingdom will be removed (see below).

```{r}
# Identify OTUs that should only be assigned to the kingdom level
otu_BLAST_assign <- BLAST_unknown[["taxa_OTU"]]
```

Before keeping them, let's check that these OTUs do not dominate any sample, by visualizing the proportion of their reads in each sample:

```{r}
# Proportion of reads belonging to these OTUs in each sample
unknown_prop <- data.frame(
  sample_data(otu_BLAST_filter),
  prop_unknown = sample_sums(prune_taxa(otu_BLAST_assign, otu_BLAST_filter)) /
    sample_sums(otu_BLAST_filter) * 100)

ggplot(unknown_prop, aes(x = SiteID, y = prop_unknown)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0, size = 1) +
  labs(x = "Site", y = "Reads of OTUs with uncertain BLAST matches (%)") +
  theme_bw()
```

In all samples, these OTUs represent a small proportion of the reads, thus keeping them will not affect community analyses.

### Rank-level confidence

Now that we are confident about our OTU selection, it is time to clean the taxonomy assignation. BLASTn searches preferentially for highly identical regions, and thus might cut off the ends of a synthetic sequence (not a real ITS fragment) yielding a maximal-scoring segment pair with lower query coverage and higher percentage identity, thus falsely classifying it as a real ITS match. Therefore, we must verify the `pident` to decide if we can trust the BLAST results. The table below summarizes thresholds for each target gene and taxonomic rank found in the literature.

+----------------+----------------+--------------------+-------------------+-------------------------+--------------------+
| Taxonomic rank | ITS\           | ITS\               | 16S\              | CO1\                    | CO1\               |
|                | (cons.)        | (rot)              | (cons.)           | (cons.)                 | (cons.)            |
+================+================+====================+===================+=========================+====================+
| Kingdom        |                | 70 [@tedersoo2019] |                   |                         |                    |
+----------------+----------------+--------------------+-------------------+-------------------------+--------------------+
| Phylum         |                | 75 [@tedersoo2019] | 75.0 [@yarza2014] | 78\* [@pappalardo2025]  | 85 [@ransome2017]  |
+----------------+----------------+--------------------+-------------------+-------------------------+--------------------+
| Class          | 80.9 [@vu2019] | 75 [@tedersoo2014] | 78.5 [@yarza2014] | 78\* [@pappalardo2025]  | 90 [@timmers2020]  |
+----------------+----------------+--------------------+-------------------+-------------------------+--------------------+
| Order          | 81.2 [@vu2019] | 80 [@tedersoo2014] | 82.0 [@yarza2014] | 87\* [@pappalardo2025]  | 92 [@timmers2020]  |
+----------------+----------------+--------------------+-------------------+-------------------------+--------------------+
| Family         | 88.5 [@vu2019] | 85 [@tedersoo2014] | 86.5 [@yarza2014] | 90^†^ [@pappalardo2025] | 96 [@timmers2020]  |
+----------------+----------------+--------------------+-------------------+-------------------------+--------------------+
| Genus          | 94.3 [@vu2019] | 90 [@tedersoo2014] | 94.5 [@yarza2014] | 95^†^ [@pappalardo2025] | 98 [@timmers2020]  |
+----------------+----------------+--------------------+-------------------+-------------------------+--------------------+
| Species        |                | 98 [@tedersoo2021] | 98.7 [@kim2014]   | 98^†^ [@pappalardo2025] | 100 [@timmers2020] |
+----------------+----------------+--------------------+-------------------+-------------------------+--------------------+

: Table 3. Thresholds for taxonomy identification. "cons." = conservative threshold identified in a study; "rot" = arbitrarily defined rule of thumb. Notes: \* Thresholds with 1-5% error rates; ^†^ Thresholds with \>5% error rates.

Based on the thresholds identified in Table 3, any taxonomic assignation below these thresholds will be changed to `NA`. For example, for an OTU identified to the species level, but that only has a `pident` of 95%, there is no certainty on the taxonomic assignation up to that rank. However, a `pident` of 95% allows for certainty up to the genus level. Thus, for this OTU, we would simply remove the assignation at the species level (replace it with `NA`) and preserve the other ranks.

For ITS, we use the rules of thumb of Tedersoo et al. ("ITS (rot)" in Table 3): species 98%, genus 90%, family 85%, order 80%, class 75% and phylum 75% [@tedersoo2014; @tedersoo2019; @tedersoo2021]. In the ITS reference database, ranks without assignation are written as `.`: we first replace them with `NA`, so that all missing assignations are written the same way.

```{r}
#| output: false
# Clean the OTU table based on taxonomy thresholds
# (remove assignation if confidence is too low).
BLAST_clean <- BLAST_filter %>%
  # Replace missing assignations (".") with "NA"
  mutate(across(phylum:species, ~ if_else(.x == ".", "NA", .x))) %>%
  mutate(species = if_else(pident < 98, "NA", species),
         genus = if_else(pident < 90, "NA", genus),
         family = if_else(pident < 85, "NA", family),
         order = if_else(pident < 80, "NA", order),
         class = if_else(pident < 75, "NA", class),
         phylum = if_else(pident < 75, "NA", phylum)) %>%
  # Remove uncultured assignation
  mutate(across(phylum:species, ~ gsub(".*uncultured.*", "NA", .x))) %>%
  # Remove metagenome assignation
  mutate(across(phylum:species, ~ gsub(".*metagenome.*", "NA", .x))) %>%
  # Remove assignation below kingdom for previously identified OTUs
  mutate(across(phylum:species, ~ if_else(taxa_OTU %in% otu_BLAST_assign, "NA", .x)))
```

How many OTUs are assigned to each rank, before and after cleaning?

```{r}
# Before cleaning
colSums(BLAST_filter[, c("phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species")] != ".")

# After cleaning
colSums(BLAST_clean[, c("phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species")] != "NA")
```

The cleaning mostly affects the lowest ranks: about one third of the species assignations are removed, as well as the phylum assignation of the uncertain OTUs identified above.

The cleaned taxonomy table (`BLAST_clean`) should now be put back into the OTU table (`phyloseq` object).

```{r}
# Replace taxonomy table in the phyloseq object
otu_BLAST_clean <- otu_BLAST_filter
otu_BLAST_clean@tax_table <- tax_table(as.matrix(BLAST_clean))
```

### Save the OTU table

```{r}
#| eval: false
# OTU table with cleaned taxonomy, based on BLAST accuracy
save(otu_BLAST_clean, file = "RData/ITS/otu_BLAST_clean.RData")
```
